# opwan_address_assignment (Resource)

Where one of the account's addresses is routed: down a tunnel, to BGP, or nowhere. Moving an address is instant and free, and its firewall follows it. An address bought in a block moves with its whole block, so manage one address per block. Destroying this resource leaves the address where it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opwan_address_assignment" "web" {
  ip        = "72.244.89.11"
  kind      = "tunnel"
  tunnel_id = opwan_tunnel.office.tunnel_id
}

# Floats to whichever BGP tunnel announces it.
resource "opwan_address_assignment" "anycast" {
  ip   = "72.244.89.12"
  kind = "bgp"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip` (String) One of the account's addresses (dotted IPv4).
- `kind` (String) `tunnel` (routed down `tunnel_id`), `bgp` (goes to whichever of the account's BGP tunnels announces it, dropped while none does) or `unassigned` (kept, traffic to it dropped).

### Optional

- `tunnel_id` (String) The tunnel to route the address down (`tun_...`). Only with `kind = "tunnel"`.

### Read-Only

- `block` (String) The block the address was bought in (`72.244.89.16/30`), null for a single address.
- `id` (String) The address, same as `ip`.
- `location` (String) The address's location id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import opwan_address_assignment.web 72.244.89.11
```
